name: COLLECTIVE STOCK 16-category independent critic rubric
purpose: Score an implementation against world-class stock-media interaction quality without copying competitor trade dress.

anchors.5: Functional prototype quality with obvious friction, omissions, or weak evidence.
anchors.7: Solid production baseline but materially behind the benchmark or inconsistent across routes/devices.
anchors.8: Strong professional implementation with a small number of meaningful gaps.
anchors.9: World-class execution: complete, consistent, evidence-backed, accessible, fast, and clearly native to Collective AI.
anchors.9.3: Approval threshold for the weighted overall score, provided every hard gate and per-category floor also passes.
anchors.10: Exceptional and demonstrably better for the target use case; no material defect found after adversarial review. A 10 requires evidence, not aesthetic enthusiasm.

calculation.rounding: Report two decimal places. Do not round up before applying the 9.3 threshold.
calculation.approval_rule: Approve only if the weighted score is at least 9.30, every category is at least 9.0, and every hard gate passes. A high average cannot offset a hard-gate or category-floor failure.

hard_gates.pass_condition: Final unassigned-assets manifest is an empty array and audit reconciliation proves every discovered occurrence has a provenance record and visible route.
Automated validation reports zero broken original, optimized, poster, logo, video, and rendition references.
Parent gallery, complete archive, every required collection, and all 20 division routes render real manifest data without placeholder-only content.
No critical WCAG 2.2 A/AA defect remains; dialogs, search, filters, cards, and media controls complete keyboard and screen-reader task flows.
Private/internal originals cannot be fetched from a public static URL and are delivered only after authorization using a protected or signed mechanism; private pages are excluded from indexing.
No material defect blocks search, filters, navigation, detail viewing, playback, licensing, or download on representative small and large mobile viewports.
Representative mobile public pages meet LCP <= 2.5 s, CLS <= 0.1, INP <= 200 ms and Lighthouse Performance >= 90, Accessibility >= 95, Best Practices >= 95, SEO >= 95 under a documented test profile.
No generic placeholder substitutes for an accessible real project asset; all explicitly missing project assets are listed in a missing-asset report rather than concealed.

categories.name: First impression
categories.review_question: Within five seconds, does the product read as a premium, trustworthy Collective AI media library with an obvious next action?
required_evidence: five-second test notes from at least three reviewers
categories.score_9_definition: The brand, product purpose, access context, search action, and real-media quality are immediately legible; no placeholder, loading jank, or generic template signal is visible.
categories.score_10_definition: The opening view is memorable and uniquely Collective AI while loading quickly and preserving task clarity across desktop and mobile.

automatic_ceiling.condition: Hero uses a generic/duplicated asset, the primary action is ambiguous, or initial layout shift is visible.

categories.name: Visual hierarchy
categories.review_question: Do hierarchy, spacing, density, typography, and contrast guide users from search to collection to asset without visual competition?
categories.score_9_definition: Primary, secondary, and tertiary actions remain distinct on every core route; dense grids stay scannable; metadata is available without overwhelming imagery.
categories.score_10_definition: Hierarchy adapts elegantly by task and viewport while maintaining cinematic restraint and zero ambiguity.

automatic_ceiling.condition: Gold/teal/accent usage competes with assets, multiple CTAs have equal weight, or metadata becomes unreadable at any supported viewport.

categories.name: Brand distinctiveness
categories.review_question: Is the experience unmistakably Collective AI while avoiding a palette-swap treatment of divisions and avoiding competitor imitation?
required_evidence: at least six contrasting division pages
categories.score_9_definition: Parent identity follows the supplied design system; every division has approved identity, voice, geometry, and behavior while sharing a coherent system; no copied proprietary layout is evident.
categories.score_10_definition: The design establishes a defensible, reusable visual language that feels more appropriate to the governed Collective AI archive than any public-stock reference.

automatic_ceiling.condition: Division differentiation is mainly accent-color swapping or any fabricated logo replaces an approved mark.

benchmark_patterns: do not reproduce competitor headers, pricing cards, iconography, or signature page proportions

categories.name: Homepage quality
categories.review_question: Does the homepage successfully support known-item search, inspiration, division entry, recent media, motion discovery, licensing comprehension, and access awareness?
categories.score_9_definition: Search dominates appropriately; actual media powers the mosaic and rails; divisions, collections, recent media, motion, access state, and licensing are all reachable without bloating the page.
categories.score_10_definition: The homepage balances editorial surprise and operational efficiency better than a generic commercial stock homepage for this archive.

automatic_ceiling.condition: Any required homepage section is absent, uses placeholders, or repeats the same assets enough to imply a shallow library.

categories.name: Search usability
categories.review_question: Can users quickly find an exact asset or a useful conceptual set across titles, divisions, categories, prompts, tags, colors, aspect ratios, uses, media, licenses, and revisions?
required_evidence: query test set with expected results
categories.score_9_definition: Search is fast, scoped, typo-tolerant, highlighted, URL-synchronized, keyboard accessible, and returns credible ranked results with suggestions, counts, recent searches, and clear reset.
categories.score_10_definition: Literal and semantic intent are transparently handled, ranking is explainable enough for governed assets, and expert search remains efficient at archive scale.

automatic_ceiling.condition: Filters are not reflected in the URL, key manifest fields are unsearchable, result counts are inaccurate, or keyboard users cannot complete search.

benchmark_patterns: Shutterstock AI/standard mode clarity and related queries

categories.name: Gallery browsing
categories.review_question: Do grids, cards, filters, sorting, quick preview, favorites, and pagination/infinite loading make large, mixed-format libraries easy to scan?
categories.score_9_definition: Cards maintain aspect integrity, expose essential media/license data, support Save/Preview/Similar without hover dependence, and remain stable and fast through large collections.
categories.score_10_definition: Browsing feels effortless across images, sheets, vertical video, motion, and 3D while retaining provenance and revision relationships.

automatic_ceiling.condition: Visible unintended duplicates exist, cards crop critical content, infinite loading loses position, or essential card actions are hover-only.

categories.name: Asset-detail experience
categories.review_question: Does each asset detail page provide the preview, metadata, provenance, rights, renditions, variants, related media, and navigation needed for a confident decision?
categories.score_9_definition: Large preview, zoom/fullscreen, complete manifest metadata, access/license status, usable renditions, original download, variants, related media, copy link, and previous/next are cohesive and accessible.
categories.score_10_definition: The page supports both rapid internal reuse and rigorous provenance/legal review without switching tools or losing search context.

automatic_ceiling.condition: License or visibility is separated from the download action, original/rendition data is inaccurate, or revision/occurrence provenance is hidden.

categories.name: Division differentiation
categories.review_question: Do all 20 division pages and the parent gallery express their correct identity and content while remaining one product system?
categories.score_9_definition: All required routes work from the real manifest; identity, hero, editorial voice, geometry, collections, and related divisions vary meaningfully; counts reconcile with the archive.
categories.score_10_definition: Division personality changes the experience in useful, content-aware ways without reducing consistency or accessibility.

automatic_ceiling.condition: Any division route is missing, generic, incorrectly branded, or populated from fabricated/repeated assets.

benchmark_patterns: Use public platforms for reusable gallery mechanics only; division differentiation is a unique COLLECTIVE STOCK requirement.

categories.name: Mobile experience
categories.review_question: Can a touch user complete navigation, search, filtering, preview, detail, playback, licensing, and download on representative mobile devices?
required_evidence: real-device or high-fidelity emulation task run
categories.score_9_definition: Navigation and filters use intentional mobile patterns; controls meet target size; grids adapt without crop/overflow; dialogs and media handle safe areas, orientation, and keyboard correctly.
categories.score_10_definition: Mobile is a first-class media workflow, including vertical video, gestures with equivalent controls, fast search, and interruption-safe state.

automatic_ceiling.condition: Desktop mega-menu/filter UI is merely compressed, horizontal overflow occurs, or any core action depends on hover.

benchmark_patterns: Do not infer competitor quality; require direct evidence. Use sticky scoped search and progressive filter sheets as appropriate.

categories.name: Video and motion handling
categories.review_question: Are video, animated previews, motion backgrounds, vertical media, posters, captions, fallback, and reduced-motion behavior production-ready?
categories.score_9_definition: Poster-first media uses playsinline, safe muted autoplay only when intended, accessible controls, viewport pausing, preview concurrency limits, no layout shift, static fallback, and cleanup.
categories.score_10_definition: Motion materially improves discovery while staying quiet, efficient, captioned where needed, and fully usable under reduced motion or network failure.

automatic_ceiling.condition: Any media autoplays with sound, ignores reduced motion, continues offscreen, lacks an accessible pause, or breaks without video support.

benchmark_patterns: Adobe duration/quality and explicit play signals

categories.name: Licensing clarity
categories.review_question: Can a user understand access level, license type, permitted/restricted uses, attribution, approval requirements, and delivery consequences before download?
required_evidence: license UI for every required license type
categories.score_9_definition: Rights are concise and adjacent to the action; full terms are available; internal/public/restricted status is enforced at delivery; approval and attribution are unambiguous.
categories.score_10_definition: The rights model makes complex internal and public use safer and faster than the public-stock references while preserving complete audit history.

automatic_ceiling.condition: Private assets rely on CSS hiding or a disabled button, a license is missing, or an original public URL bypasses authorization.

categories.name: Accessibility
categories.review_question: Does the product meet WCAG 2.2 AA and support complete keyboard, screen-reader, reduced-motion, zoom, and touch workflows?
categories.score_9_definition: Zero critical defects; landmarks/headings/labels are accurate; focus is visible and restored; dialogs trap appropriately; alt text is asset-specific; media controls and filters are operable; 200% zoom/reflow works.
categories.score_10_definition: Accessibility is editorially and operationally excellent, including provenance-rich alt text policy, robust error announcements, and assistive-technology efficiency at archive scale.

automatic_ceiling.condition: A critical WCAG defect exists, a core flow is keyboard-inaccessible, or private/error states are not announced.

benchmark_patterns: skip links and labeled landmarks observed on Shutterstock/Envato
avoid carousel clones in the accessibility tree

categories.name: Performance
categories.review_question: Does the implementation meet its mobile Core Web Vitals and Lighthouse targets with real manifest scale and mixed media?
categories.score_9_definition: All stated targets pass on representative public pages; responsive images, explicit dimensions, poster-first video, lazy loading, immutable assets, and limited priority prevent jank and waste.
categories.score_10_definition: Performance remains comfortably within budget across homepage, large archive, division, search, and detail routes on representative mobile hardware and poor networks.

automatic_ceiling.condition: Any required target misses, asset optimization upscales/overcompresses incorrectly, or gallery/video loading causes memory/interaction degradation.

benchmark_patterns: Competitor richness is not a performance exemption; use their progressive disclosure, not their page weight.

categories.name: Conversion design
categories.review_question: Do calls to action move internal and public users toward the correct next step without obscuring rights or using dark patterns?
categories.score_9_definition: Internal users optimize for correct reuse/download, public users see value and license before authentication, restricted users get a safe next step, and CTAs remain truthful and well prioritized.
categories.score_10_definition: The product converts through confidence, relevance, and rights clarity while preserving editorial calm and user control.

automatic_ceiling.condition: Registration blocks metadata/preview prematurely, upgrades are preselected ambiguously, or public/internal calls to action are indistinguishable.

benchmark_patterns: avoid Depositphotos-style acquisition gating for authorized internal users

categories.name: Professional credibility
categories.review_question: Does the product demonstrate trustworthy provenance, accurate counts/metadata, secure delivery, resilient states, SEO discipline, and production readiness?
categories.score_9_definition: Counts reconcile, metadata is accurate, provenance is inspectable, security/SEO/access controls are correct, failures recover gracefully, and the build/test/deploy path is documented and repeatable.
categories.score_10_definition: The platform behaves like a governed DAM and premium public catalog simultaneously, with defensible evidence for every trust claim.

automatic_ceiling.condition: Audit math fails, security headers are absent, private content is indexed/exposed, or completion claims exceed evidence.

categories.name: Overall desirability
categories.review_question: After completing representative tasks, would expert internal users choose this product as the fastest, safest, and most inspiring way to use Collective AI media?
categories.score_9_definition: The experience is coherent, fast, distinctive, complete, and worth returning to; no unresolved weakness materially lowers trust or task success.
categories.score_10_definition: The product creates preference through a uniquely strong combination of archive completeness, brand intelligence, search quality, and rights confidence—not surface spectacle.

automatic_ceiling.condition: Any critic weakness remains unaddressed without evidence-based disposition, or the experience feels like a themed clone of a benchmark platform.

benchmark_patterns: Synthesize best interaction principles; do not average competitor aesthetics or imitate trade dress.

overall: links to screenshots, reports, and test output
prohibitions: Do not award points for unverified claims.
Do not let visual polish offset inaccessible, insecure, missing, or unreconciled assets.
Do not treat competitor resemblance as quality.
Do not approve your own implementation work.
Do not call a revision complete without rerunning its verification method.
